scope: Where the expert formal model (formal/) departs from the source documents. Only the formal model and the documents are compared; results/, claims/ and flow/ are not part of this file. Entries marked material=false were found in passing; the minor list is not exhaustive.

categories.contradiction: The formal model does something the documents rule out.
categories.convention: The formal model fixes a choice the documents leave open or do not state.
categories.scope: The formal model contains content that is not in the documents.

doc_check.confirmed: The quoted text was checked in the document, or the document was searched and is silent on the point.
doc_check.pending: Not yet confirmed against the whole document set.

formal.excerpt: in(c, (SAr1: SA_t, SAr2: SA_t, IDi: host, IDr: host)); ... let (=IDi, AUTHi: bitstring, SAi2: SA_t, TSi: bitstring, TSr: bitstring) =

document.quote: Responders MUST select a single complete set of parameters from the offers (or reject all offers if none are acceptable).

entries.description: The responder reads its child SA (SAr2) from the network at process start, independently of the SAi2 it receives; SAi2 is parsed but never used. The document says the responder selects SAr2 from the initiator's offer.

formal.excerpt: out(c, mac(senc((IDi, AUTHi, SAi2, TSi, TSr), SK_ei), SK_ai));

document.quote: The optional payload IDr enables the initiator to specify to which of the responder's identities it wants to talk.

entries.description: The optional [IDr] payload of IKE_AUTH message 3 is always omitted, so the responder never learns or checks the identity the initiator intended. The document makes the payload optional and lets the responder finish with another IDr.

document.quote: initiator of an exchange MUST check that the accepted offer is consistent with one of its proposals

entries.description: The initiator requires message 4 to echo its own SAi2, TSi and TSr byte-for-byte (and SAr1 = SAi1). The document has the responder choose one proposal and allows traffic-selector narrowing; the initiator only checks consistency with its proposals.
